title: Ericsson transforms 5G indoor connectivity at its new Spain headquarters
summary: Ericsson Radio Dot bring high-capacity 5G and seamless indoor coverage to Ericsson’s Madrid headquarters.
body_markdown:
Ericsson (NASDAQ: ERIC) has deployed its Radio Dot indoor system throughout its new headquarters in Madrid, transforming the company’s new space into a live hub for innovation. The six-floor building is a working demonstration of dependable indoor mobile connectivity, keeping people connected as they move between floors, meeting rooms and the outdoors.


Most mobile traffic today is generated indoors, yet the challenge for modern buildings is no longer simply to provide coverage. The indoor connectivity paradigm is shifting from being connected everywhere to delivering the right capacity in the right place. Demonstration and customer-experience areas have different traffic needs from employee workspaces, so the network is designed to distribute capacity where activity and digital interaction demand it most.


The design draws on Ericsson Mobility Report forecasts and Ericsson’s dimensioning work for the site. Ericsson Mobility Report 2025 data, when the design of Madrid office started, show continued growth in mobile data traffic, with total mobile data traffic forecast by that time to increase from 123 EB per month in 2024 to 280 EB per month, meaning traffic is expected to reach around 160% of today’s level, in 2030. For Madrid offices design, this growth outlook has been translated into an estimated 80 GB per employee per month by 2030, creating the basis for a future-ready indoor network dimensioned for capacity as well as coverage.


Built on Ericsson Radio Dot, the system combines compact radio units with a shared multi-operator design using a Multi-Operator Radio Access Network (MORAN) approach. Capacity can be increased centrally through the Indoor Radio Unit (IRU) layer, adding sectors without changing the installed Radio Dots. The required equipment can be housed in a single rack, avoiding significant additional technical space and power consumption compared with traditional Distributed Antenna System-based approaches.


The deployment supports:


- Seamless continuity and security between indoor and outdoor coverage.
- High capacity aligned to demand: up to 4.5 Gbps in high-demand areas such as the demonstration center and up to 3.5 Gbps in employee workspaces.
- Central capacity expansion without disrupting the installed Radio Dot footprint.
- The ability to prioritize selected users, services, or applications to support service levels when the network is busy or in specific circumstances.


The network is also designed for evolving enterprise traffic. As collaboration tools, cloud applications and AI-enabled experiences generate more uplink traffic, the design based on capacity has also considered the expected uplink traffic demand. Ericsson’s ambition is for 5G to provide employees, visitors and enterprise devices with secure, seamless and consistent connectivity not only based on current traffic profiles but also for future demands.


Ericsson aims to roll out 5G connectivity across its corporate PCs, supporting employees working both in and outside the office. The initiative is intended to enable Ericsson IT teams to centrally provision and manage eSIMs, while helping establish secure, reliable connectivity aligned with corporate policies.


“Ericsson’s new office in Madrid is more than a new address,” says Juan Olivera, Head of Ericsson Spain. “It’s our commitment to the country and to continue building a story of innovation in Spain. Our new office brings this ambition to life through Ericsson’s state-of-the-art 5G indoor connectivity solutions deployed across the premises, enhancing the experience for our people and visitors.”


The same principles apply to public buildings, transport hubs, security and critical-communications sites: indoor networks must be designed for capacity, uplink readiness, continuity and security—not only basic coverage. Ericsson’s headquarters deployment offers a template for one shared, high-capacity indoor network that distributes capacity intelligently and prioritizes what matters most.
